chapters.s: The water level of the Kamala-Balan falls, and the village confronts a new age of environmental crisis. Satyanarayan began planting new trees around Channa Grove—not only for memory, but for nature. With the village youth he repaired the pond embankment, dug small catchments to hold rainwater…

chapters.t: The Miracle of the Handheld Phone
chapters.s: The arrival of the mobile phone completely changes communication in the village. Remembering the warning, Anjali taught the village elders to use mobile phones—how to speak with a son, how to see his face. At the same time she kept telling every household that however near a machine might bring the…

In the age of the IT boom, the village’s educated youth seek new opportunities in the markets of great cities. From that day on, however busy he was, Karunakar spent one evening of every annual visit beneath the pipal, telling the village children stories of the city and listening to their old village stories.…

The Right to Information Act gives the village the power to demand its records and its history officially. Using the Right to Information law, Vibha obtained every available old official record of the village’s land and history and brought them together with Yadavanand’s shadow-register.…

The employment-guarantee programme gives village labourers local work and stability. Remembering the warning, Suresh kept the accounts of every project transparent. Every worker’s name, every day of attendance, every wage payment was displayed openly before the village so no name could be omitted and no…

The arrival of smartphones and the internet transforms village life in both good and harmful ways. Remembering Budhba’s warning, Neeraj formed a small village youth group where they learned together to verify every suspicious claim seen online—which news was true or false, which offer genuine or fraudulent.…

chapters.t: The First Shadow on the Screen
chapters.s: By Neeraj’s time, Facebook and WhatsApp had reached nearly every hand in the village. Relatives living far away seemed close again, old friends found one another once more, and news of every joy and sorrow in the village could reach everyone in moments. Sapna gave a new form to the women’s old tradition of night assemblies and created a “digital night assembly” for the women and girls of the village, where stories of online harassment and fraud could be shared openly and confronted together.…

chapters.t: The First Footfall of the Unseen Swindler
chapters.s: In Sapna’s time, a young man from the village, lured by the promise of a job, lost all his savings to a fraudulent online company. The company had seemed genuine—it had a website, photographs of an office, the voices of supposed officials. That very night, keeping Budhba’s words in mind, Sapna began teaching every family in the village how to guard against online fraud—which offers were genuine and which were false, where it was safe to send money and where danger lay.…

After Sapna, the responsibility for the ritual passed to her son Rajiv. In Rajiv’s time, fraud carried out through false promises of employment took an even more terrible form. From that day, Rajiv began teaching every young person in the village how to examine offers of work abroad—which agent was genuine and which a fraud, which document was real and which false, where it was safe to go and where danger waited.…

In Rajiv’s time, a child was born into a poor family in the village. The household rejoiced in the ordinary ways—a sohar was sung, jaggery was distributed, and the child was named Ujjwal Jha. Hearing this, Deepali wrote Ujjwal’s name in her notebook beside the record of every new birth in the village, adding an extra mark so that no one in the future would forget it.…
